answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a stake-and-score gate per agent identity. To open one, an agent locks a bond larger than one epoch of expected earnings, and payouts scale with a score that grows only from settled, reviewed jobs. A newcomer starts at zero and earns little until real work clears. This is an orchard rule: each identity is a tree planted with locked stake that needs seasons of history before bearing fruit, and every record is public. A fake result forfeits the bond and resets the score, so cloning costs copper, not upside. The fable of endless yield from clones breaks on cost.
